newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Davids sees steady year earnings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Davids sees steady year earnings.

text.p: Grocery wholesaler Davids Ltd said on Tuesday its earnings for the year to end-June 1997 were expected to equal to the 1995/96 result.
"Earnings are expected to be equal with last year, this year," Davids joint managing director Jeff David told reporters
Davids earlier reported a half year net profit for the six months to December 31, 1996 of A$24.15 million, down from A$29.24 million in the previous corresponding period.
The company said profit before goodwill amortisation, interest and tax rose A$7.6 million to A$69.1 million, showing the underlying strength of the business.

The lower net result reflected increased amortisation of goodwill following the acquisition of QIW Ltd in 1996, a disappointing performance from the Cash & Carry division; and one-time costs related to the amalgamation of QIW, it said.

Davids said Campbells Cash & Carry reported a loss of A$3.2 million for the six months and flagged little improvement in the second half. "There will however be a return to profitablility during fiscal 1998," David said in a media briefing.

The company believed Campbells remained a viable business but a review was likely to lead to the closure and relocation of a number of brances, and the merger of others into the John Lewis Foodservice business.
Gross sales at John Lewis rose 56 percent to A$215 million, while the retail division recorded sales of A$698 million.
Australian Liquor Marketers (ALM), 50 percent owned by Davids, lifted gross sales 28 percent ot A$961 million.
David said Woolworths had informed the company they would stop using ALM, but said he believed that New Zealand operations would in time replace the loss.
Woolworths purchases amounted to about A$150 million, against gross projected annual sales of A$1.5 billion, he said.
The distribution division lifted gross sales 39 percent to A$1.91 billion.
Davids shares ended down two cents at A$1.52.
